title: How Mantises Kill Huge Prey 😨

title_pattern.template: How <Small Animal> <Verb> <Surprisingly Big Thing> + fear emoji
title_pattern.notes: Zack D. Films house format: 'How X Does Y' process promise, 4-5 words, Title Case, one emoji (😨) as the emotional label. Size inversion (mantis vs 'huge prey') is the curiosity gap. No numbers, no clickbait caps.

thumbnail.source: auto-selected video frame (~16 s), shown letterboxed in the 16:9 thumb with blurred zoomed copies on both sides; no custom design
thumbnail.composition: Centre-weighted 9:16 frame: mantis upright in upper half, lizard head horizontal across lower-middle, rock floor at bottom, burned-in caption 'to its mouth' just above the floor
thumbnail.text: Only the burned-in caption 'to its mouth' (white bold sans with soft shadow); no title text
thumbnail.colours: Three flat fields: saturated cyan-blue sky, lime/leaf green insect, brown scaly lizard, mauve-pink rock; complementary green/blue vs warm brown/pink, very high clarity
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Predator smaller than prey yet dominating it - mantis looms above the lizard's head from a low camera; lizard eye and open jaw read as fear
thumbnail.why_it_works: In the Shorts feed the thumbnail barely matters; the first frame does. The frame still communicates the whole premise (bug eating lizard) with photoreal macro texture and a clean sky background, so it reads at tiny sizes.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: As the lizard approaches, it snaps its leg around its body. And because those
hook.device: In-medias-res action cold open: no question, no 'did you know', no intro - the first word is the story already happening ('As the lizard approaches') with the predator already in frame and the strike landing at ~1.5 s. The title supplies the question; the video starts straight on the answer. Ending ('eating the lizard alive') sits right before the opening line so the Short loops seamlessly into a rewatch.
hook.visual: Frame 0 already shows both animals face to face in photoreal 3D; first motion event (the strike) at 1.2 s, first cut at 3.3 s.

beats.summary: Lizard approaches; mantis instantly snaps a foreleg around it. Action before explanation.
Why the grip works: forelegs lined with rows of sharp spines that sink into the skin; visual escalates from wide to macro of spines in scales.
Prey thrashes but can't escape - 'no matter how much it struggles' tension beat.
'Then the mantis pulls it up to its mouth' - process moves to next step; thumbnail frame.
Jaws work like tiny slicing blades - crash push into mouthparts, carving off a piece.
'one tiny piece at a time, eating the lizard alive' - shock kicker on the final word, calm wide tableau, loops back to the opening line.

pacing.caption_chunking: 1-4 words per caption, swapped every ~0.5-1 s, word-group not word-by-word; always centred at ~70% height
pacing.sentence_structure: 6 sentences, each a causal link: 'As...', 'And because...well,...', 'And no matter how...', 'Then...', 'And since...'. Every sentence starts with a connective, so there is never a full stop in momentum.
pacing.music: Low continuous ambient/tension music bed under VO (auto-subs tag [music]); no stingers detected; mean loudness -14.8 dB, peak 0 dB
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: ~3.5-4 s: every new clause comes with a new camera angle, and each mechanism gets a macro reveal (spines at 7 s, mouthparts at 18 s)

techniques_worth_copying: Start mid-action with a connective ('As the X approaches,'): no setup, the title carries the question.
Chain every sentence with causal connectives (because / no matter how / then / since) so it plays as one unbroken process.
Mechanism -> macro shot: each time the VO names a body part (spines, jaws), the camera crash-pushes into an extreme close-up of exactly that part.
Emphasis glow: tint the named feature (spines go red/orange) for a beat so the eye lands on it.
Hide every cut inside a whip pan / foreground body wipe, so the 25 s plays like one continuous camera.
Simple 3-colour world (blue gradient sky, mauve rock, green subject) gives instant readability and makes the subject pop.
End on a shock word ('alive') on a calm wide, with the last line flowing grammatically into the first for a seamless loop.
Underdog scale inversion in the title (small predator, 'huge prey') plus a single emotion emoji.
Captions: short white bold sans chunks with soft drop shadow, mid-lower frame, never covering the subject's face.

code_only_remake_needs.feasibility: Medium-hard. The appeal is photoreal 3D creature texture, which SVG can't match; a code-only remake has to swap realism for a bold stylised illustration look and keep the structure, camera language and pacing.
code_only_remake_needs.assets: Layered SVG creatures (mantis: head, thorax, two raptorial forelegs with separate spine rows, antennae; prey: body, head with hinged jaw, legs) built for rigging; separate high-detail 'macro' SVGs for the spine row on skin and the mouthparts, so crash-ins cut to purpose-drawn close-ups rather than scaling a low-detail sprite.
code_only_remake_needs.rig_animation: Simple bone rig in Remotion (rotate groups around pivots) for the foreleg strike (fast ease-out snap ~6 frames), lizard walk cycle, struggle shake, mandible open/close loop; spring() for the snap overshoot.
code_only_remake_needs.camera: Virtual camera wrapper (scale + translate + small rotate) with presets: slow orbit (parallax between sky/rock/creature layers), push-in, crash push (scale 1->3 in 8-10 frames, ease-in), handheld noise (perlin offset 2-6 px), and whip transition (horizontal directional blur via SVG feGaussianBlur stdDeviation x-only or a CSS blur + 40-80 px slide over 6-9 frames).
code_only_remake_needs.environment: Full-bleed vertical linear gradient sky (#2aa7e8 -> #8fd8f5), mauve rock plane with noise texture (feTurbulence), ground horizon low in frame for low-angle shots.
code_only_remake_needs.fx: Emphasis glow on named parts (fill tween to red-orange + feGaussianBlur glow), small red droplet particle falling, depth-of-field fake via blurred foreground layer.
code_only_remake_needs.captions: Word-timed captions from TTS alignment, 1-4 word chunks, white bold rounded sans (e.g. Montserrat/Inter 800), soft shadow, centred at ~70% height.
code_only_remake_needs.audio: Kokoro/Piper VO at ~175-180 wpm with calm documentary narrator delivery, low ambient tension music bed; total 22-30 s.
code_only_remake_needs.storyboard: 6 beats / 13 shots / ~19 visual changes in 25 s; every VO clause triggers a new camera preset; final line written to flow into the first line for looping.
